item.title: AusFitness Expo Melbourne 2026: Everything You Need to Know Before You Go
item.description:
AusFitness Expo Melbourne 2026: Everything You Need to Know Before You Go

Australia’s biggest fitness expo is back at MCEC this Saturday and Sunday (March 21–22), and whether you’re a gym regular, a fitness professional, or just someone who enjoys watching very strong people do extraordinary things — it’s worth knowing what you’re walking into before you get there.

Here’s the full rundown on AusFitness Expo Melbourne 2026: what’s on, what it costs, and how to make the most of it.

item.title: Best Bars in Collingwood 2026: Live Music, Craft Beer and Late-Night Haunts
item.description:
Best Bars in Collingwood 2026: Live Music, Craft Beer and Late-Night Haunts

Collingwood doesn’t do boring drinks. Squeezed between Hoddle Street and Smith Street, this pocket-sized suburb packs more bars per square metre than most Melbourne postcodes — and every single one has a personality. Sticky-floored punk temples sit three doors from natural wine havens. Craft breweries share laneways with cocktail bars that seat twelve people and nothing more.

If you’re heading to Collingwood for a night out in 2026, this is where you should be drinking.

item.title: Best Restaurants in Collingwood 2026: Where Locals Actually Eat
item.description:
Collingwood doesn’t do subtle. The strip between Smith and Johnston streets packs more personality per square metre than anywhere else in Melbourne — converted warehouses, street art on every laneway, and a restaurant scene that refuses to pick a lane. Fine dining sits next to $9 tacos. Rock’n’roll pizza joints share walls with Japanese soba specialists.

Here’s where to eat in Collingwood right now, ranked by people who actually live here.

item.title: Melbourne Food & Wine Festival 2026: The Only Guide You Actually Need
item.description:
The Melbourne Food & Wine Festival is back from March 20 to 29, 2026, with over 200 events across the city. That’s ten days of long lunches, pastry pop-ups, barbecue throwdowns, and enough degustation menus to bankrupt your savings account.

But you don’t need to wade through 200 events. You need to know which ones are actually worth it. Here’s our no-fluff guide.

The Free Stuff (Yes, Free)

Something Saucy: The Pizza Party — March 26

The lads from Super Norma in Carlton — Luca Muscato and Marco Salzano — are giving away 1,000 free slices of pizza at Leonardo’s Pizza Palace. The pizza? Eggplant, tomato and cheese, riffing on their namesake pasta alla Norma. Oh, and there are 800 free Bloody Marys for anyone who reckons 11:30am on a Thursday is cocktail o’clock.

item.title: 15 Best Cheap Eats in Carlton Under $20 — Student-Approved, Wallet-Friendly
item.description:
Here are the 15 best cheap eats in Carlton for 2026, every single one under $20. From hand-folded dumplings and Malaysian rice bowls to Neapolitan pizza slices and Bhutanese momos, Carlton’s student-driven food scene means you eat brilliantly without thinking about your bank balance. This guide covers Lygon Street, Grattan Street, Elgin Street and the laneways in between.

What’s inside:

  • Dumpling dealers: Aunty’s Dumplings, Shanghai Village, HuTong
  • Noodle temples: Hakata Gensuke, Lagoon Dining
  • Pizza by the slice: DOC, Garfield Pizzeria, Leonardo’s
  • Global budget bangers: Rice Bar, Taquito, Panda Hot Pot
  • New openings 2026: Aunty’s Dumplings, Garfield Pizzeria, Florian To Go

Carlton has a secret weapon that no other Melbourne suburb can match: a permanent population of approximately 30,000 university students who demand excellent food at prices that won’t bankrupt them before mid-semester exams. The result is one of the most competitive budget dining strips in Australia, where restaurants know that a $25 main means empty tables while a $15 bowl means a queue out the door.

item.title: 18 Best Cafes in Carlton for Coffee, Brunch and Everything in Between
item.description:
Here are the 18 best cafes in Carlton for 2026, from Lygon Street Italian institutions to Japanese lamington labs and specialty roasteries. This guide covers every corner of Melbourne’s coffee capital, with venues spanning Berkeley Street’s warehouse roasteries to Rathdowne Street’s leafy neighbourhood spots. Whether you’re after a traditional espresso, matcha perfection, or wild‑fermented bagels, Carlton delivers.

What’s inside:

  • Coffee institutions: Seven Seeds, Market Lane, University Cafe
  • Italian classics: DOC, Pidapipó, Brunetti Classico
  • Japanese‑Australian fusion: Tokyo Lamington, Attakai
  • Neighbourhood essentials: Baker D. Chirico, Florian, Rathdowne Street Cafe
  • All‑day venues: Sleepy’s Cafe & Wine Bar, Assembly

There’s something beautifully chaotic about Carlton’s cafe scene. Walk down Lygon Street on any given morning and you’ll find Italian nonnas arguing over espresso strength outside century-old institutions while twenty-somethings queue for $22 avo toast at the latest specialty roaster. This is a suburb where Melbourne’s coffee obsession began — University Cafe has been pulling shots since 1952 — and where it continues to evolve, with Japanese lamington labs and third-wave coffee temples sitting side by side.

item.title: 19 Best Bars in St Kilda for Every Kind of Night Out
item.description:
St Kilda’s bar scene runs from legendary music venues where international acts have graced the stage to intimate wine bars hidden down laneways, rooftop cocktail spots with bay views, and dive bars that feel like your local even on your first visit.

What’s covered in this guide:

  • The Icons: Essential St Kilda institutions including The Espy and Prince Public Bar
  • Rooftop & Waterfront: Beach-adjacent venues with killer views and coastal vibes
  • Wine Bars & Cocktail Spots: Intimate spaces for serious sipping and conversation
  • Pubs & Live Music: Where to catch gigs and settle in for a proper session
  • Local Favourites & Late-Night: Neighbourhood gems and after-midnight options

There’s something magical about St Kilda after dark. Maybe it’s the way the fairy lights strung along the Esplanade catch the bay breeze, or how Luna Park’s neon glow spills across Fitzroy Street as revellers bounce between venues. This bayside suburb has been Melbourne’s playground since the 1850s, and that party spirit lives on in every corner pub, rooftop bar, and laneway wine dive.

item.title: 19 New Melbourne Restaurants, Bars and Bakeries to Try in March 2026
item.description:
Melbourne’s hospitality machine never stops. Here are 19 new restaurants, bars and bakeries that opened in February and March 2026 — from a Tokyo ramen institution making its Australian debut to a mother-daughter dumpling shop in Carlton, a CBD Lune flagship and a Korean burger joint that’s already generating serious hype.

What’s inside:

  • International arrivals: Ginza Kagari (Tokyo ramen), Gaon (ex-Nobu Korean)
  • Carlton renaissance: Garfield Pizzeria, Aunty’s Dumplings, Bar Carnation, Florian To Go
  • CBD power moves: Lune flagship, Seoul Tiger 1988, Apa’s Canteen
  • Inner suburb gems: Santito (Collingwood tacos), Brewpub Huzzah (Glen Iris)
  • Late-night & drinking: Miscellania rooftop, Blackhearts & Sparrows Fitzroy, Otoya at Crown

Melbourne added 19 new venues to its already ridiculous dining scene in the past month. Some are international arrivals that chose Melbourne over Sydney (always satisfying). Some are neighbourhood joints born from lockdown hustle. A few are straight-up bucket list additions. All of them are worth your time and money right now.

item.description:

item.title: 23 Best Restaurants in Fitzroy You Need to Try in 2026
item.description:
Here are the 23 best restaurants in Fitzroy for 2026, from hatted fine dining to hidden neighbourhood gems. This guide covers every corner of Melbourne’s most diverse food suburb, with venues across Brunswick, Gertrude, and Smith Streets. Whether you’re after Andrew McConnell’s legendary dry-aged beef, authentic Filipino breakfast, or charred miso ramen, Fitzroy delivers.

What’s inside:

  • Fine dining: Cutler, Marion, Gaea, Carnation Canteen
  • Neighbourhood essentials: Poodle, Norma, Alta Trattoria, Bar Liberty
  • International flavours: Añada (Spanish), Toddy Shop (Indian), Masti (Punjabi), Palay (Filipino)
  • Casual classics: Belles Hot Chicken, Vegie Bar, Mario’s, Rice Paper Scissors
  • Specialty spots: Ramen Ako’s, Gogyo (ramen), Deep End Pizza, Tamura Sake Bar

Forget what you think you know about Fitzroy. Yes, it’s still got that artsy edge that made it famous, but the food scene here has evolved into something extraordinary. This isn’t your mate’s share house suburb anymore — it’s Melbourne’s most democratic dining destination, where a $9 banh mi from a hole-in-the-wall shares the same street as hatted restaurants charging $240 for dry-aged beef.

item.title: AITMA: 5 Melbourne Dilemmas That Will Divide Your Group Chat
item.description:
Am I The Melbourne A-Hole? Five real Melbourne scenarios. You vote. No mercy.

AITMA #1: The Brunch Betrayal

My friend raves about this cafe in Fitzroy — “best brunch in Melbourne, you HAVE to go.” So I went. The eggs were fine. The toast was fine. Everything was… fine.

When she asked what I thought, I said: “Yeah, it was alright. Nothing special though.”

She hasn’t spoken to me in four days.

item.title: An Honest Guide to South Yarra: Where Your Wallet Goes to Die
item.description:
South Yarra. The suburb that thinks it’s Bondi but with worse weather and more expensive parking.

Let’s be honest about this place.

The Vibe

South Yarra’s vibe is “I definitely can’t afford this but I’m going to pretend I can.” Every second person is wearing activewear that costs more than your weekly rent. The other half are wearing activewear that costs more than your monthly rent.

The median age is 28. The median bank balance is concerning. The median confidence is off the charts.
